candidate.title: BSAS
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina BSAS schematic: a single linear preparation of targeted bisulfite amplicons followed by transposome-mediated tagmentation to DNA fragments. BSAS expands to bisulfite amplicon sequencing; Nextera XT is the embedded library-preparation component, not a separate target method. The leftmost methylation-marked BSAS title cartoon is descriptive, not another branch. Primary-paper context explains the C/T methylation readout and the downstream dual-indexed library interface; unshown indexing, sequencing and analysis are not added as depicted operations.

states.label: Methylated DNA
features: Genomic DNA containing methylated cytosines is the substrate; the biological target is cytosine methylation in selected genomic regions.
The input is drawn as a blue line with red marks. A similar yellow-ringed motif accompanies the far-left BSAS title; the image supplies no separate chemical legend for these colors.

evidence.quote: BSAS involves; (1) bisulfite conversion of genomic DNA to distinguish between methylated and unmethylated cytosines, (2) PCR amplification of regions of interest with PCR primers specific for converted sequences, (3) transposome mediated (Nextera XT) NGS library preparation technology, (4) sequencing the amplified regions on a benchtop sequencer (Illumina MiSeq), (5) alignment to in silico converted reference sequences, and 6) application of variant-calling algorithms for counting of cytosines and thymines at CpG sites for quantitative digital methylation analysis (Figure 1).

states.label: Amplicons
features: Paired blue lines depict DNA amplicons produced from selected regions of bisulfite-converted genomic DNA.

PCR copies encode originally unmethylated cytosines as T and originally protected cytosines as C. Thus sequence differences, rather than preservation of the original methyl groups in PCR copies, carry the methylation information.

evidence.quote: Therefore, in sequence analysis of bisulfite-converted DNA, methylated cytosines appear as cytosine and unmethylated cytosines appear as thymines.
evidence.rationale: The paper states that uracils become thymines upon PCR and that converted-DNA sequence analysis yields C at protected sites and T at unmethylated sites; the amplicon sequence therefore carries the original conversion history.

states.label: DNA fragments derived from the targeted bisulfite amplicons
features: The Tagmentation cartoon shows blue DNA with orange terminal segments, followed by an arrow to stacked blue lines labeled DNA.
Primary-paper-supported interpretation: tagmentation fragments the amplicons and attaches adapters. The terminal sequences, strand polarity and detailed end chemistry are not resolved by this icon.
This boundary is the tagmentation product. The paper separately adds dual indexes by PCR after tagmentation, so the drawing alone does not establish completed dual-indexed sequencing libraries.

The fragments carry sequence representations of the selected bisulfite-converted regions. In the completed primary implementation, C/T counts at reference CpG sites provide base-specific methylation estimates. This is targeted coverage, not a whole-genome methylome or separate quantitation of 5-mC and 5-hmC.

operations.label: Bisulfite conversion
operations.description: Convert genomic DNA to bisulfite-treated DNA: unmethylated cytosines are deaminated to uracil while methylated cytosines remain unconverted in the primary-paper account.
operations.mechanism: Bisulfite-induced deamination establishes differential sequence behavior of unmethylated and protected cytosines; the figure depicts the conversion as one broad operation.
operations.information_effect: Transfers the original cytosine modification status into a chemical difference readable after amplification. Conversion resistance is not a uniquely specific 5-mC readout: the paper states that 5-hmC can contribute.

operations.label: PCR with primers specific for bisulfite converted DNA
operations.description: Amplify selected regions of the converted genomic DNA using primers specific for bisulfite-converted sequences, producing DNA amplicons. Uracils introduced by conversion become thymines in the amplified DNA.
operations.mechanism: Target-specific PCR enrichment of bisulfite-converted templates, not an assay that selectively amplifies only methylated molecules.
operations.information_effect: Restricts the represented genome to primer-defined regions and propagates C/T sequence encoding of the original cytosine state. Downstream C/T counts estimate methylation at covered positions; the primary paper identifies original bisulfite-PCR bias as a potential limitation.

evidence.locator: Discussion, [b00033], limitations
evidence.quote: Limitations of the BSAS method, as described here, could arise from (1) PCR bias in the original bisulfite specific PCR, (2) bias in the transposome-mediated DNA fragmentation and adapter ligation, (3) and the inability of BSAS to distinguish between 5-mC and 5-hmC.

operations.label: Tagmentation
operations.description: Act on the bisulfite-derived PCR amplicons with the adaptor-bearing transposome to generate smaller adapter-bearing DNA fragments. The transposome is a reagent/catalyst input, not an amplicon-derived product.
operations.mechanism: Transposome-mediated simultaneous DNA fragmentation and adapter attachment, identified as the Nextera XT component by the primary paper and catalogue description.
operations.information_effect: Produces fragment inserts from targeted amplified regions while retaining the C/T sequence information. In the complete primary workflow, subsequent index PCR associates reads with samples, and sequencing/alignment enables C/T counting; those downstream operations are not drawn here. The paper reports reduced sequence depth near amplicon ends, attributed to reduced likelihood of transposome insertion there.

method_scopes.rationale: The diagram title names only BSAS; page 76 is a verified matching catalogue page headed BSAS: Bisulfite Amplicon Sequencing. Masser et al. explicitly describe this order of bisulfite conversion, PCR of converted sequences, and Nextera XT transposome-mediated library preparation. Sequencing and dual indexing contextualize the library/readout but are outside the drawn transformation graph.
